Chapter Five: Guarding Time and Living with Intention.
You know, time really is the one thing we can never get back. If we lose money, we can earn it again. If we misplace our favorite things, chances are we’ll replace them at some point. But hours and days? Once they slip away, they’re gone. It’s easy to forget that in the middle of our busy, noisy lives, but this truth sits right at the heart of what makes life meaningful.
Picture this: someone spends years putting off their dreams, always assuming there’s plenty of time in the future. One day, it hits them—the future isn’t promised. So, they choose to make a change. Not with one big, sweeping gesture, but through a string of small, deliberate decisions. They start saying no to things that don’t really matter. They set boundaries around their time, focusing on what truly brings them joy and fulfillment. It’s not always easy. There are doubts, and plenty of moments where old habits try to creep back in. But slowly, a new kind of freedom starts to grow—a satisfaction that can’t be faked.
Guarding your time doesn’t mean you have to be selfish or inflexible. Really, it’s about recognizing just how valuable each day is, and choosing to spend it on what counts. This means being honest with yourself about what actually brings you happiness and meaning, and having the courage to let go of everything else. It’s about making room for the things that feed your spirit—like nurturing relationships, getting creative, learning something new, or just giving yourself space to rest.
Living with intention? It takes discipline and a lot of self-awareness. It’s so easy to fall back into old routines, or let other people’s demands decide how you spend your time. But when you make a real effort to guard your hours, you’ll notice life feels deeper, richer, and more satisfying. There’s this sense of control and purpose that comes from knowing you’re using each day well.
And look, this isn’t about being perfect. Distractions are always going to pop up. There’ll be setbacks, and yes, you’ll have moments where you slip. The trick is to keep coming back to one simple question: Am I spending my time on what truly matters? If you make that question part of your daily life, it gets easier to stay focused, and to stay intentional.
The rewards? They’re bigger than you might think. Your relationships deepen. Your work starts to feel more meaningful. And there’s a sense of peace that comes from knowing your time isn’t being wasted. Life almost feels longer—not because you have more years, but because every year is filled with purpose and real joy.
